base_stage: M7 FIX5 automated Windows gate pass candidate
decision: FIX6 CANDIDATE - WINDOWS TWO-CLIENT CONVERGENCE RERUN REQUIRED

problem_evidence.visible_symptom: multi-second movement/network freeze while item actions were occurring
problem_evidence.diagnosis: realtime observability remained allocation-heavy on server and graphical clients: telemetry observe duplicated/shifted bounded arrays, transport telemetry allocated default dictionaries per packet, both sides rebuilt full transport boundary snapshots at frame rate, and dirty server READY reports could materialize a full runtime report every 250 ms

production_changes: network_telemetry_collector.observe now appends until full and then overwrites an in-place ring slot; it no longer duplicate()s the sample window or shifts the oldest element on the realtime path
steady-state telemetry lookups avoid eager default Array/Dictionary allocation for existing distributions and transport channels
M7 dedicated server keeps cheap gauges frame-current but samples full transport boundary peer statistics at 4 Hz instead of every process frame
M7 graphical client does the same 4 Hz transport peer-stat sampling instead of rebuilding the full boundary snapshot every frame
M7 READY diagnostic report materialization is coalesced to at most 1 Hz while initial READY and terminal reports remain synchronous
SERVER_HEALTH exposes current/peak server process, report-build and peer-telemetry durations
PREDICTION_HEALTH exposes current/peak graphical-client process and peer-telemetry durations
correctness_invariants: FIX4 retained transient authority time unchanged
NX3 input wire schema and pressure compaction unchanged
Item Graph delta plus reliable gameplay revision synchronization unchanged
FIX5 server-authoritative frozen WORLD replica policy unchanged

synthetic_hot_loop.note: Synthetic single-process microbenchmark only; it demonstrates the cost class removed from observe(), not end-to-end server throughput.

two_client_failure_evidence.diagnosis: the two clients converged to the same gameplay checksum, but the process worker compared them with the throttled READY file's embedded snapshot. FIX6 deliberately reduced READY materialization to 1 Hz, so that diagnostic snapshot can be older than the runtime's explicit last_two_connected_checksum capture. This is an acceptance-fixture synchronization defect, not evidence of peer gameplay divergence.

correction.worker_policy: prefer server last_two_connected_checksum; fall back to snapshot.checksum for older runtimes
correction.required_next_step: rerun the FIX6 graphical-client focused test and the full two-client process gate

required_windows_gate: FIX6 editor import/composition PASS on Godot 4.7.1.stable.double.custom_build.a13da4feb
FIX6 server realtime hot-path regression PASS
FIX6 graphical client telemetry/convergence-fixture regression PASS

long_manual_acceptance.actions: continuously move/turn while repeatedly dropping, picking up, splitting, stacking and transferring items from both clients
requirements: no sustained pending input growth into the dozens
scheduler backlog may rise transiently but returns to zero and dropped_time_seconds remains zero for stalls below the configured one-second retention window
prediction lead returns to the normal low-single-digit range instead of remaining in tens/hundreds of ticks
no hard multi-metre reconciliation correction and no visible backwards pull
SERVER_HEALTH and PREDICTION_HEALTH timing fields make any remaining server/client slow-frame source attributable
ANALYZE_M7_FIX6_STRESS.ps1 returns PASS under the chosen acceptance thresholds

assistant_execution.note: The Windows gate confirmed the FIX6 focused runtime changes but exposed a process-fixture convergence check that read a stale throttled READY snapshot. The worker/test correction is committed; the two-client rerun remains authoritative.
